But the announcement states this is a firm-fixed-price foreign military sales contract and names the customers — Iraq, Jordan, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and Qatar — so the missiles are being bought for them, not for the Army line. The 'other procurement funds' obligation does not identify an Army appropriation clearly enough to overturn the FMS framing stated on the face of the award.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for 356 High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicles
proposals.lexicon_quote: HI MOB MULTI-PURP WHLD VEH (HMMWV)	3446D15400	346	HI MOB MULTI-PURP WHLD VEH (HMMWV)
proposals.rationale: The announcement writes the vehicle name out in full where the index row abbreviates it, and AM General is the HMMWV producer, so the name match is real. The award is explicitly a modification to a foreign military sales (Iraq) contract for 356 vehicles delivered to that customer; 'other procurement funds' is named but the buy is not the Army's own. The index also carries an ARNG HMMWV Modernization Program under a separate code, a second reason not to assert which line a foreign buy would have executed.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for night vision sensor systems, subcomponent production and technical services for the Apache attack helicopter
proposals.lexicon_quote: AH-64E	5757A05111	343	AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman
proposals.rationale: Rejected under §3's first pattern: the Apache is the platform the contract supports, not the program the line funds. The only Apache name this index carries is AH-64E under the Block IIIA remanufacture line, which buys remanufactured aircraft; this award buys night vision sensor subcomponents and technical services from Lockheed Martin at Orlando, the MTADS/PNVS sight house, and the sight itself appears nowhere in the index. The announcement also states that work locations and funding will be determined with each order, so there is no appropriation evidence to test.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for Modernized Target Acquisition Designation Sight/Pilot Night Vision Sensor kits and spares for the Apache Attack Helicopter
proposals.lexicon_quote: AH-64E	5757A05111	343	AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman
proposals.rationale: Same §3 platform rejection. The program the award actually names is MTADS/PNVS, which this org's index does not carry under any code; 'Apache Attack Helicopter' is the airframe the kits and spares are fitted to. Attaching a sight-kit-and-spares buy to the AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman line would assert that aircraft remanufacture money paid for it, which the announcement does not say — it names only fiscal 2017 'other funds'.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to deliver a realistic, high-end collective training experience at the Joint Readiness Training Center at Fort Polk
proposals.lexicon_quote: Combat Training Centers Support	1780MA6600	346	Combat Training Centers Support
proposals.rationale: Rejected under §3 as generic services. The Joint Readiness Training Center is a place, not a program in this index, and the tempting Combat Training Centers Support row names an OPA line that buys instrumentation and surrogate vehicles — opposing-force vehicles, threat air defense systems, training ASE suites — not a contractor-delivered training experience. The obligation is fiscal 2022 operation and maintenance, Army funds, which is O&M attached to a procurement line: the money-and-mission failure mode, on top of the name not actually being present.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for the AH-64 Apache Modernized Target Acquisition Designation Sight/Pilot Night Vision Sensor Performance Based Logistics program
proposals.lexicon_quote: AH-64E	5757A05111	343	AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman
proposals.rationale: Two independent §3 grounds. The named program is an MTADS/PNVS performance-based logistics arrangement, which this index does not carry; the AH-64 is the platform being sustained. And the funding is fiscal 2024 Army working capital funds — depot sustainment recovered through rates — which cannot be evidence that an aircraft procurement line's own work was paid for.

proposals.program_name: The M88 Heavy Equipment Recovery Combat Utility Lift and Evacuation System (HERCULES)
proposals.announcement_evidence: for logistics support and training for M1A1 Tanks and M88 recovery vehicles for the government of Iraq
proposals.lexicon_quote: The M88 Heavy Equipment Recovery Combat Utility Lift and Evacuation System (HERCULES)	3700GA0570	350	IMPROVED RECOVERY VEHICLE (M88 HERCULES)
proposals.rationale: Rejected on two §3 patterns at once. The work is logistics support and training — generic services — and the M88 and M1A1 are platforms the services are wrapped around, not the recovery-vehicle procurement the line funds. It is also a foreign military sales modification performed for the government of Iraq with funding and work location undetermined, so nothing here asserts that the Army's Improved Recovery Vehicle line executed a dollar of it.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for Apache attack helicopter depot-level support
proposals.lexicon_quote: AH-64E	5757A05111	343	AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman
proposals.rationale: Rejected under §3: 'Apache attack helicopter depot-level support' names a platform and a support activity, with no program at all. The AH-64E row belongs to the Block IIIA remanufacture procurement line, and the obligation is Army working capital funds, the depot sustainment color. Linking this would publish the claim that aircraft procurement paid for depot support, which the announcement contradicts.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to procure single channel ground and airborne radio systems
proposals.lexicon_quote: Single Channel Data Radio (SCDR)	6458B95004	349	Handheld Manpack Small Form Fit (HMS)
proposals.rationale: This is the string-similarity trap the identity lens exists to catch. 'Single channel ground and airborne radio systems' is SINCGARS, a legacy Harris combat-net radio family; the only index row that looks like it is the Single Channel Data Radio, a waveform-bearing radio inside the Handheld Manpack Small Form Fit program. Sharing the words 'single channel' does not make them the same program, and SINCGARS has no row in this index. Note the lexicon_doc I have transcribed here should read 346 as it does in the index row; the proposal is wrong regardless of that field.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for the Glide Breaker Phase 2 program
proposals.lexicon_quote: Common Hypersonic Glide Body (CHGB)	2611C72100	345	LONG-RANGE HYPERSONIC WEAPON
proposals.rationale: Rejected on identity and on org. Glide Breaker is a DARPA effort to intercept hypersonic vehicles — the contract number HR0011-23-C-0044 is a DARPA PIID and the award cites a Broad Agency Announcement — while the Common Hypersonic Glide Body is the Army/Navy glide vehicle that Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon fields. They share the word 'glide' and nothing else; one is the threat-side interceptor, the other is the offensive body. Proposing an Army line for a DARPA award would attach the money to the wrong organisation entirely.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for Abrams systems technical support
proposals.lexicon_quote: M1A2 System Enhancement Package (SEP)	6500GA0750	350	Abrams Upgrade Program
proposals.rationale: Rejected under §3 twice over: 'Abrams systems technical support' is generic engineering support, and Abrams is the platform the support attends to rather than a program this index names. No name from the Abrams Upgrade Program narrative — SEP, TIGER, ADL, FLIR, COE, DSESTS — appears in the announcement; the M1A2 SEP row is only the nearest candidate an unchecked matcher would reach for. That fiscal 2021 'Army procurement appropriation funds' are named does not rescue an award whose description identifies no program.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for the AH-64 Apache Modernized Target Acquisition Designation Sight/Pilot Night Vision Sensor Performance Based Logistics program
proposals.lexicon_quote: AH-64E	5757A05111	343	AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman
proposals.rationale: Identical in form to the other MTADS/PNVS performance-based-logistics record on this contract, and rejected for the same two reasons: the program named is the sight's PBL arrangement, which this index does not carry, and the Apache is the platform it sustains. Fiscal 2023 Army Working Capital funds confirm this is depot sustainment, not the aircraft procurement 5757A05111 funds.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for modernized target acquisition designation sight/pilot night vision sensors and its subcomponents on the Apache 64D/E helicopter
proposals.lexicon_quote: AH-64E	5757A05111	343	AH-64 Apache Block IIIA Reman
proposals.rationale: The 'D/E' in 'Apache 64D/E helicopter' makes this the most tempting of the Apache records for a designator matcher, and it is still wrong: the item bought is the MTADS/PNVS sight and its subcomponents, which this index does not carry, and the airframe designator is only telling you which aircraft they mount on. It is also a Foreign Military Sales order for India and Taiwan with funding determined per order, so even the platform reading would not put the money on the Army's remanufacture line.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for Stryker sustainment services
proposals.lexicon_quote: Stryker Double-V-Hull (DVH)	0363G85200	350	Stryker Upgrade
proposals.rationale: Rejected under §3 as generic services on a platform name. 'Stryker sustainment services' names the vehicle family and a support activity; none of the Stryker Upgrade narrative's own names — DVH, DVHA1, ICVVA1, MCWS and the rest — appears, and the Double-V-Hull row is only the nearest thing a name matcher would grab. Work locations and funding are undetermined, so there is no appropriation evidence either. The contrast with the double-V-hull conversion record I did link is exactly the line §3 draws.
